title: Scenario playbook: Model trajectory and procurement triggers (2025-2027)
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Objective: Produce a concise scenario playbook that maps credible model-supply trajectories (availability, pricing, quantization readiness, licensing change) across 2025-2027 and define procurement/rollout triggers Redwood PMs and Partnerships should use. Deliverables: 1) Three scenario narratives (Baseline, Market Shock, Opportunity Acceleration), 2) Quantified trigger thresholds (latency/cost/availability), 3) Recommended procurement actions (reserve, defer, hybrid-fallback), 4) Monitoring signals and watchlist indicators for automated alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Three scenario narratives documented with clear assumptions and probabilities
Trigger thresholds defined and mapped to concrete actions (reserve capacity, activate Dedicated trials, enable quant fallback)
Signal list (metric + source) compiled and integrated with the model-watch pipeline
Executive one-pager and ops runbook approved by GTM and Infra leads
Hand-off checklist for Solutions and Sales with customer-facing messaging templates
notes: Why this matters: procurement windows and model availability timelines materially affect our Dedicated capacity commitments and customer SLAs. A playbook avoids ad-hoc decisions during supply shocks. Key trade-offs considered: commit early to obtain capacity discounts vs. over-committing to soon-to-be-obsolete model variants; prefer multi-vendor fallback to reduce single-supplier lock-in but increase ops complexity. Methodology: combine supplier roadmap signals, public pricing moves, telemetry (token latency/cold-start rates), and primary interviews with 3 suppliers and 5 enterprise customers. Use stochastic scenarios with simple probability weights for prioritization.
